- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot upward momentum, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral.
- Underestimate downward corrections after strong upward moves; model fails to recognize mean reversion when sentiment turns negative or weak.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.6), model overreacts to short-term volatility and forecasts higher prices than true outcome.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.3), model underestimates downside risk and fails to adjust downward, leading to persistent underprediction.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period, forecast still holds high values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent price action and ignores longer-term trend, leading to overfitting to recent highs/lows.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/–), model tends to average out extremes, resulting in smoother forecasts that miss sharp reversals.
- Correct for “sentiment-driven bias”: if sentiment is rising, model should not ignore recent price momentum; if sentiment is falling, model should not ignore recent price drop.
